title: A reversible auxiliary channel selects one comparator for the original nonnormal power average

statement.quantifiers: Every finite bistochastic r-self-compatible Phi, r>=2, and integer n>=0; no normality or selfadjointness.
statement.assertion: One canonical Psi has I-Psi<=kappa(I-Phi*Phi),kappa=2r/(r-1), and averaged EB insertion Lambda_n approximates Phi^n in induced HS by sqrt(kappa/(n+1)).
assumptions: Bistochasticity makes Phi* a legal channel and Phi an HS contraction.
Actual all-output postprocessing witnesses Phi*Phi compatibility.

outputs: One C8 binary comparator and EB averaged-power approximation for original Phi.
interface.precision: Exact finite HS inequality; correct binary2/sqrt(n+1).
costs: POVM selection compact/nonconstructive, acquisition/precision/output costs separate.
Reversible original theorem retains its sharper coefficient and finite-n expression.

proof_mechanism: Postprocess broadcaster outputs Phi* to select Theta=Phi*Phi.
Average one EB insertion over n+1 positions, apply Jensen and left HS contraction.
Original-orbit norm losses telescope exactly, no functional calculus or Psi commutation.
obstructions: Cannot drop unitality/TP and assume the adjoint remains a channel.
No diamond upgrade; an early draft binary constant was corrected before source release.

potential_uses.transfer_gate: Select a comparator from an actually compatible adjoint square and telescope on the original dynamics.

review.source_reported: Source reports internally reconstructed mathematics with scoped independent analytic audits; finite checks are not proof certification; no independent ingestion proof reconstruction, scientific replay, external correctness or priority clearance.
